{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mo-f","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"68e256815d3b4ce4d037d8edbc1bd14dc15d69bff2158f2288a6404a10a7b0c9","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mo-class-f:lineage:101","source_registry_sha256":"f128002157e581eb7004b9370c8cfbafd7b29a1596262980704fbda0a45932f5","source_liveness_sha256":"fdf72d02e75b9589fee5aaf5b83ec9705ff03586f574464e3553a827f9b698d8"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Missouri rules of the road: right-of-way, passing, emergency vehicles, school buses, signals, turns and roundabouts","heading":"C — Rules of the road: duty of care, passing on the right and left, right-of-way, emergency vehicles, school bus stops, signals, turns, U-turns and roundabouts","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Rules of the road: duty of care, passing on the right and left, right-of-way, emergency vehicles, school bus stops, signals, turns, U-turns and roundabouts
Knowledge domain: the general duty of care, when passing on the right or moving left of center is allowed or forbidden, who yields at intersections and roundabouts, what to do for moving and stopped emergency vehicles and school buses, signaling distance, turn lanes, U-turns and roundabout conduct.

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
A motorist's highest duty is careful, prudent driving, with speed and manner that keep the road safe for pedestrians, cyclists and other drivers as well as yourself. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Right-of-way law only says who must yield and never gives any driver the right-of-way, so you must do everything possible to avoid striking a pedestrian or vehicle no matter the circumstances. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
Speeding or passing in a construction or work zone on Missouri state roads can bring a fine of at least $250 for a first offense and at least $300 for any later offense, on top of other fines. [A01]
Why it matters: dynamic detail: fine amounts are set by statute and can change.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
Pass a pedestrian or cyclist with the same care as a motor vehicle, slowing and waiting for a safe chance just as you would behind any slow traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
Passing on the right is allowed when the vehicle ahead is turning left or about to, or on a city street with clear pavement wide enough for two or more lines of vehicles each way. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
Passing on the right is also allowed on a one-way street, or on a highway outside a city with clear pavement wide enough and marked for four or more lanes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
Passing on the right may never be done by leaving the paved main roadway and driving on the shoulder. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
Do not move to the left side of the road when nearing a hill crest or curve where your view is blocked enough that an oncoming vehicle would create a hazard. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A01
Do not drive left of center within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel when your view is obstructed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A01
Do not drive left of center within 100 feet of or at an intersection or railroad grade crossing, or anywhere a solid yellow line is present. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A02
Drivers yield as needed to avoid hitting pedestrians crossing legally, and anyone crossing a sidewalk or entering or leaving a driveway, alley or parking lot yields to pedestrians; driving on a sidewalk is illegal except to cross it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A02
A driver turning left yields to oncoming vehicles going straight. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A02
At a four-way stop, the driver who reaches the intersection first goes first, after stopping completely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A02
A driver entering a road from a driveway, alley or the roadside yields to vehicles already on the main road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A02
At an intersection with no stop sign or signal, other than a roundabout, yield to vehicles coming from your right. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A02
Approaching a roundabout, yield to traffic already circulating and to pedestrians in the crosswalks, and wait for a gap before entering. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A02
Yield to police, fire, ambulance and other emergency vehicles using a siren or air horn with a red or blue flashing light by pulling to the right edge of the road, or as near as possible, from whichever direction they come. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A02
If you are already in an intersection, drive through it before pulling over, stay stopped until the emergency vehicle passes, follow loudspeaker instructions, and move on only when the way is clear because more may follow. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A02
Nearing a stopped emergency vehicle showing red or red and blue lights on a road with at least four lanes and two or more going your way, move with caution into a lane not next to it if that is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A02
If changing lanes away from a stopped emergency vehicle would be unsafe or impossible, slow down and keep a speed that is safe for conditions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A02
A school bus flashes amber warning lights 500 feet before a designated stop, then shows alternating flashing red lights and its stop arm once stopped. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A02
When the bus's red lights and stop arm are on, oncoming and following traffic must stop before reaching it on a two-lane road with traffic both ways and on a two-lane one-way street. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A03
You need not stop when traveling the opposite way on a divided highway whose directions are on totally separate roadways, the opposite way on a highway of four or more lanes, or when the bus is in a school loading zone where students do not cross. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A03
After stopping for an unloading school bus, watch for children along the roadside and stay stopped until the bus moves or its driver signals you on, then proceed with caution. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A03
A conviction for failing to stop for a school bus loading or unloading students carries five points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A03
Failing to stop for a school bus brings a court-ordered suspension of 90 days or as the court sets for a first offense, 90 days for a second offense within 5 years, and 180 days for a third or later offense within 5 years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A03
Signal before stopping, turning or changing lanes using hand and arm signals or your turn signals and brake lights, and check often that the vehicle signals work. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A03
Move into the proper turn lane and signal at least 100 feet before a turn, and look both ways for oncoming traffic and pedestrians first. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A03
With no signs or lane markings, turn from the lane nearest the direction you are heading into the lane nearest the one you left, then change lanes afterward if needed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A04
Make a U-turn only when safe, never on a curve or near a hill crest where others may not see you, never at a No U-Turn sign, and never at an intersection controlled by a signal or police officer; some towns ban them. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A04
Turning from a one-way street onto a two-way street, start in the left lane and enter to the right of the yellow dividing line, using the right lane of a four-lane road if it is free. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A04
Turning from a two-way street onto another two-way street, keep your left wheels as close as possible to the yellow line and enter to the right of the center line, using the right lane of a four-lane road if it is free. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A05
With two left-turn lanes, a car in the left-side turn lane enters the left lane just right of the yellow line, and a car in the right-side turn lane enters the right lane. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A05
Enter a center two-way left-turn lane only to slow or stop before a left turn from the main road, never travel in it more than 500 feet, and never use it when entering from a side street. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A05
At a roundabout you make a slight right turn and travel counterclockwise around the center island, yielding to traffic in the circle, bicyclists and pedestrians in the crosswalks. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F36 | anchor: A05
Slow down before a roundabout, follow signs and markings to the correct lane in a multi-lane one, look left as you approach, and never make a left turn to enter. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F37 | anchor: A06
While driving through a roundabout, keep right of the center island, yield the right-of-way to circulating vehicles, never change lanes or try to pass any vehicle, and do not stop unless stopping is the only way to avoid a crash [A06].
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F38 | anchor: A06
Leave a roundabout at a slow speed with your right turn signal on, and do not speed up until you are past the exit's pedestrian crossing. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F39 | anchor: A06
Do not enter a roundabout when an emergency vehicle is approaching, and if one comes while you are inside, exit immediately and pull to the right. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0029]

Misconceptions: the law never gives anyone the right-of-way, it only says who must yield; you may not pass on the right by using the shoulder; you do not pull over in the middle of an intersection for a siren; drivers going the opposite way on an undivided two-lane road must stop for a school bus.
Mnemonics: right-hand rule at an uncontrolled intersection, the car on your right goes first; roundabouts run counterclockwise, so enter right, look left.
Glossary: right-of-way means the legal order of who must yield; roundabout means a circular intersection controlled by yield signs; two-way left-turn lane means a shared center lane used only to set up a left turn; stop arm means the sign that swings out from a stopped school bus.
Dynamic facts: work zone fine amounts are statutory and can change, and local ordinances can add speed limits, turn rules and parking controls that differ by city.
